stories.title: Chinese open‑weight AI models trained on U.S.-banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
stories.summary: A study by Will DePue of Unemployment Labs found that the weight structures of several open‑weight large language models released by Chinese firms—including DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group—match the configuration fingerprints of Nvidia’s Blackwell GPUs, which are prohibited from export to China. The same article reports that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned after acknowledging an affair with Alice Huang, who is alleged to have helped smuggle those chips.

stories.title: US pledges lower tariffs for India in pending trade deal
stories.summary: The United States told India it will apply tariffs lower than those imposed on other trading partners under the proposed agreement. The first phase will cover goods, with services to be negotiated later. The negotiations have been ongoing for nearly two years and are reported to be close to finalisation with most key issues resolved.

stories.title: India 10‑year bond yield recovers half of prior week’s drop
stories.summary: The yield on India’s 10‑year government bond rose, wiping out roughly half of the decline recorded the week before, as the market responded to still‑elevated inflation. The headline linked the move to inflation concerns, and no specific yield level or percentage change was provided in the source. This represents a partial reversal of the earlier fall.

stories.title: Razorpay, Sembcorp Green Infra get Sebi nod to float IPOs
stories.summary: Razorpay Software Ltd and Sembcorp Green Infra recently received approval from Sebi for their initial public offerings, marking a major milestone in their growth journeys. Razorpay aims to secure Rs 5,000-6,000 crore to enhance its financial services platform, while Sembcorp Green Infra plans to raise Rs 3,750 crore to bolster its renewable energy initiatives.

stories.title: Pro-government forces control Mekelle amid civilian hardship
stories.summary: Within two weeks of the war’s start, pro‑government forces entered and now control Mekelle, the capital of Ethiopia’s Tigray region. A local hair‑salon owner, Firut Me’ar, says residents cannot meet basic needs, with many unable to feed their children and morale low. She reports that most businesses are almost non‑existent, leaving the city’s economy severely weakened.
stories.why: It shows how quickly the conflict has disrupted civilian livelihoods and created urgent humanitarian concerns.

stories.title: Uneven monsoons and possible El Nino may raise food inflation, keeping RBI rate‑hike options open
stories.summary: A Nuvama Institutional Equities report says that uneven monsoon patterns and the prospect of El Nino conditions could increase food‑price inflation in India’s fiscal year 2027. The report adds that this upside risk may leave the Reserve Bank of India open to an additional interest‑rate hike, even as overall inflation is expected to ease gradually.

stories.title: Democrats open inquiry into Trump-era Nvidia chip export approvals
stories.summary: On Thursday, House Democrat Richard Neal and Senator Ron Wyden announced a congressional inquiry into how the Trump administration handled exports of Nvidia’s H200 chips to China. They sent a letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick requesting that the department preserve records about the licensing and tariff arrangement described in the letter. As minority members they can request information but cannot compel testimony.
